issues.description: InterruptionFrame buffer clear is conditioned on params.fixed_audio_packet_size but isn't tied to flush-on-send semantics, leaving a stale-audio risk window
issues.detail: In `_write_frame`, when packetization is enabled and a serialized audio payload's total accumulated length is less than `fixed_audio_packet_size`, the leftover bytes remain in `_audio_send_buffer`. If a non-audio (non-bytes) payload is serialized next, the early `return` is skipped and the new payload is sent via `self._client.send(payload)` while audio remainder still sits in the buffer, causing out-of-order audio. Additionally, on shutdown/EndFrame there is no explicit flush of any final partial packet — trailing audio can be silently dropped.

issues.description: Packetization may emit zero-padded frames inconsistently — partial trailing bytes will be lost on stream end
issues.detail: The while-loop only emits full packets and keeps the remainder. There is no logic to pad with silence or flush at end-of-utterance/EndFrame, which is exactly the case media endpoints (like Vonage Audio Connector) care about. For a strict-framing endpoint this could cause cumulative drift or audible truncation at utterance boundaries.

issues.description: Renaming `audio_packet_bytes` to `fixed_audio_packet_size` is a breaking change without a deprecation alias
issues.detail: The changelog mentions a rename but the diff does not show any backwards-compatible alias or DeprecationWarning. Any downstream user already passing `audio_packet_bytes` to `FastAPIWebsocketParams` will get a Pydantic validation error after upgrade. Either keep both names with a deprecation warning for one release, or call out the breaking change explicitly in `changelog/3410.changed.md` with migration guidance.

issues.description: `serialize` returns raw bytes for audio without protocol-level pacing — packetization without timing yields bursts, not real-time framing
issues.detail: The PR description claims `optional protocol-level audio packetization to support media endpoints that require strict audio framing and real-time pacing`. The diff implements size-based chunking but does not implement real-time pacing (no per-packet sleep based on `_send_interval`/`_next_send_time`). Vonage Audio Connector and similar endpoints typically expect 20ms packets sent at 20ms intervals; the current code may emit all chunks in a tight loop, causing the receiver to buffer or drop frames.

issues.description: VonageFrameSerializer does not validate `vonage_sample_rate` against Vonage-supported values
issues.detail: InputParams docstring states common values are 8000, 16000, 24000 Hz but no validation is done. A user passing an unsupported rate (e.g., 22050) will silently get a resampled stream that the Vonage endpoint will reject or mis-decode. Add a Pydantic validator or a Literal type for safety.

issues.description: `serialize` ignores `OutputTransportMessageFrame.message` typing — passing a non-JSON-serializable payload will raise mid-stream
issues.detail: `json.dumps(frame.message)` assumes `message` is JSON-serializable. If a caller passes a dataclass/bytes/datetime, this will throw `TypeError` and bubble up to `_write_frame`, which only logs and continues — meaning the user's notify command silently fails. Either validate at construction or wrap with a try/except + warning here.

issues.description: Missing tests for VonageFrameSerializer and for `fixed_audio_packet_size` behavior
issues.detail: Neither the new serializer nor the packetization buffer logic is accompanied by unit tests in this diff. Given the subtle buffer-ordering, interrupt-clearing, and resampler interactions, this is a meaningful risk for regressions. At minimum: serialize/deserialize roundtrip for audio + DTMF + JSON events, and `_write_frame` packet boundary tests including the interrupt-clears-buffer path.

issues.description: DTMF dual-format parsing is speculative — `message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit')` may mask a real protocol mismatch
issues.detail: The comment says `Vonage may send digit in different formats, try both`, but the Vonage Audio Connector spec is fixed. Falling back across formats hides protocol drift and makes future debugging harder. Pick the documented field and warn loudly when the alternate appears, rather than silently accepting both.

issues.description: `self._sample_rate = 0` is a sentinel that can produce a divide-by-zero or invalid resample if `serialize`/`deserialize` is called before `setup`
issues.detail: If a caller invokes `deserialize` before `setup` runs, the resampler is called with target rate 0. Better to raise a clear `RuntimeError` or assert in deserialize/serialize when `_sample_rate == 0`.

issues.description: Copyright header says `2024–2025` on a file added in 2026
issues.detail: Cosmetic, but the new file's copyright year should reflect the year of authorship. Update to current year or to a maintained range.

issues.description: `if payload:` truthiness check rejects valid empty-but-meaningful frames
issues.detail: Existing pattern, not introduced by this PR, but worth noting: an empty bytes payload (`b''`) returned from a serializer evaluates falsy and is silently dropped. The new Vonage serializer already guards against this on its end, but a more defensive check would be `if payload is not None:`.

issues.description: `bytes(payload)` extra copy when payload is already bytes
issues.detail: `self._audio_send_buffer.extend(bytes(payload))` makes an unnecessary copy when `payload` is already `bytes`. `bytearray.extend` accepts a bytes-like object directly. Minor allocator pressure for hot audio paths.

dissents.topic: Whether real-time pacing should be in the transport or left to upstream pipeline scheduling

positions.position: The PR description promises real-time pacing; without per-packet timing this is a silent feature gap. Block until pacing is added or the description is amended.

Pipecat already has upstream pacing mechanisms (`_send_interval`, `_next_send_time`); the transport packetizer should be a pure framing concern. The example integration in pipecat-examples likely demonstrates the full pacing path. Ship as a framing-only primitive and document the pacing requirement separately.

dissents.topic: Whether the parameter rename is acceptable without deprecation

positions.position: Public Pydantic field names are part of the public API. Renaming without an alias is a breaking change that should bump minor/major and ship a deprecation alias.
If the prior name was only briefly available and Pipecat is pre-1.0, a clean rename with a clear changelog note is fine — clutter costs more than the migration.

dissents.topic: Whether DTMF dual-format parsing is defensive or hiding bugs

positions.position: Real-world protocol drift happens; tolerant parsers reduce support tickets and are defensible when explicit fields are tried first.
Liberal parsing of partner protocols is exactly how silent regressions accumulate. Pick the documented field, fail loudly on the alternate.

review.summary: The PR adds a Vonage Audio Connector serializer and an optional fixed-size packetization buffer in FastAPIWebsocketTransport. The serializer is mostly straightforward and well-scoped, but the packetization path has two correctness gaps worth blocking on: an early-return that doesn't account for buffer-vs-payload ordering when non-audio payloads interleave with buffered audio, and no flush/pad strategy at stream end or for trailing partial packets — both of which directly affect the strict-framing endpoints this feature targets. Secondary concerns: the rename `audio_packet_bytes` -> `fixed_audio_packet_size` is breaking without deprecation, the PR claims real-time pacing it does not implement, and there are no tests for either the new serializer or the new buffer logic. Smaller nits include input validation on `vonage_sample_rate`, speculative DTMF dual-format parsing, an uninitialized `_sample_rate=0` sentinel, and a stale copyright year. Recommend: address P0 ordering/flush issues and add focused tests; treat the rename, pacing claim, and validation gaps as P1 cleanup before merge.
